messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected for pool 'shared-gpu-3' (streaming) — p95=420ms, p99=1.2s, streaming stalls observed. Trigger: sla-monitoring.
incident-bot: Impact: ~4% of requests hitting streaming stall timeout, increased reconnects. Potential noisy tenant. Paging oncall.
oncall-anna: Ack — I'm on it. Paging eng-sre. @eng-sre-josh are you available?
eng-sre-josh: here, seeing the alert. grabbing logs. Can someone paste the affected pool dashboard link?
oncall-anna: dashboard: https://console.redwood/pools/shared-gpu-3/metrics (p95/p99 spikes starting 14:17 UTC).
eng-runtime-sam: I see KV cache evictions and host nvme writeback spikes correlated with the spike. Looks like heavy checkpointing from a tenant job.
eng-sre-josh: running quick top consumers check.
eng-sre-josh: `redwoodctl pool top-consumers --pool shared-gpu-3 --window 5m`
eng-sre-josh: output: `tenant:fastchat-42 (io_write=320MB/s, streams=12)`, `tenant:research-drop (io_write=28MB/s)`, `tenant:prod-chat (io_write=12MB/s)`
support-lee: customer-facing note: a few users reported long streaming stalls, intermittent reconnects. No error 5xx spike.
eng-runtime-sam: If fastchat-42 is checkpointing to disk it could saturate NVMe and cause host writeback stalls, which hurts streaming (p99).
eng-sre-josh: immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle blkio for offending tenant 2) migrate tenant to a dedicated pool 3) temporarily limit their batch/concurrency. Which do we prefer for live mitigation?
oncall-anna: We need fastest low-risk. Throttle blkio via cgroup sounds doable. Sam, can you apply a soft blkio limit for fastchat-42?
eng-runtime-sam: Applying soft limit now: `redwoodctl tenant throttle --tenant fastchat-42 --blkio 150MBps --reason 'emergency p99 mitigation'`
eng-runtime-sam: ✅ command accepted, applying policy to container cgroups. Monitoring metrics...
eng-sre-josh: After throttle: p95=210ms, p99=580ms — getting better but still above target for streaming p99=300ms.
eng-runtime-sam: Also enabled KV cache writeback batching to reduce write bursts: `runtimectl set kv.writeback.batch=true --pool shared-gpu-3`
eng-sre-josh: Noted. Consider proactive migration if p99 doesn't drop under 400ms in next 5m.
product-ops-ravi: Heads-up: fastchat-42 is an internal research job, low priority but heavy IO. Can we evict/migrate without customer impact?
customer-success-maya: support-lee says no external customers affected directly yet, just internal research and a couple prod streaming users seeing stalls. We should aim to avoid killing tenant if possible.
support-lee: I'll prepare a short-facing message if we need to notify customers.
eng-sre-josh: p99 now 360ms and trending down. Throttle helped. But KV cache evictions still higher than normal.
eng-runtime-sam: Suggest schedule: keep throttle in place, migrate fastchat-42 to a separate ephemeral pool overnight, and add a permanent QoS policy to prevent future preemption.
oncall-anna: Agree. For now keep throttle and keep monitoring. Josh — please run eviction trace to ensure no long-term damage.
eng-sre-josh: Running eviction trace: `redwoodctl pool trace-evictions --pool shared-gpu-3 --since 10m` — shows repeated prefix evictions aligned with tenant IO.
eng-sre-josh: I'm going to bump tenant to best-effort QoS (lower priority) which will prevent it from getting aggressive preemption tokens. Applying now.
eng-runtime-sam: Applied QoS=best-effort to fastchat-42. Also queued migration job: `redwoodctl tenant migrate --tenant fastchat-42 --target-pool ephemeral-gpu-1 --when now` (will migrate gracefully).
eng-sre-josh: Migration started. Expected handoff ~90s per replica.
eng-sre-josh: Post-migration metrics: p95=190ms, p99=260ms, KV evictions dropping.
oncall-anna: Great. Any lasting customer impact to report?
support-lee: From support channels: ~120 user reconnects during 14:17–14:25 window, no 5xx. We'll send a brief status update to impacted customers summarizing mitigation.
customer-success-maya: Send me the draft and I'll review. We'll offer a small credit if any paid customers were affected.
product-ops-ravi: Followup action items: 1) Add tenant IO thresholds for shared pools 2) Alert on NVMe writeback rate 3) Add automated throttling runbook steps 4) Consider eviction/auto-migration for high-IO background jobs.
eng-sre-josh: Filing follow-up ticket: INC-6579998000 — title: "High NVMe writeback from background tenant caused p99 streaming stalls in shared-gpu-3". Assigning to eng-runtime for remediation tasks.
oncall-anna: Thanks team. Leaving throttle and QoS in place for 1 hour to validate. If stable, we'll revert throttles. If not, keep migration policy.
incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Closed pages.
eng-runtime-sam: I'll add a permanent QoS rule and a pre-flight check for heavy checkpointing jobs to avoid landing on shared pools.
eng-sre-josh: Also adding a metric: tenant_io_write_rrate > 200MB/s for >2m should trigger preemptive migration.
support-lee: Drafted customer note: "We detected elevated streaming latencies affecting some users due to high disk IO from an internal job. We throttled the job and migrated it to an isolated pool; service latency has returned to normal. Sorry for the disruption." Sending to Maya now.
customer-success-maya: Reviewed, looks good. Send. :white_check_mark:
eng-sre-josh: closing thread after 1h stable observation. Thanks all. :pray:
